subject.title: fix(auth): cooldown inline api key billing failures

question: Should configured inline provider API keys inherit the same restart-persistent billing cooldown behavior as stored auth profiles, despite the related recovery report describing users remaining blocked after credit restoration?
rationale: The implementation correctly follows the existing profile-cooldown pattern, but extending its persisted recovery semantics to previously untracked inline keys is a user-facing auth-policy choice rather than a purely mechanical repair.

options.title: Match stored-profile cooldowns
options.body: Keep the provider-scoped persisted cooldown design, rebase the PR, and document or expose the intended recovery route for users whose billing has recovered.

options.title: Use shorter-lived inline cooldowns
options.body: Keep retry protection for inline keys but give them a separate, bounded recovery policy rather than inheriting the full persisted profile cooldown.

options.title: Pause for recovery design
options.body: Defer this PR until the persistent-cooldown recovery direction in the related report is resolved for both profiles and inline keys.

recommendation.title: Match stored-profile cooldowns
recommendation.body: Keep the provider-scoped persisted cooldown design, rebase the PR, and document or expose the intended recovery route for users whose billing has recovered.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has carried the concrete inline-key cooldown design through several repair cycles and can provide the implementation context for the maintainer policy decision.
